explicitExclusions.reason: The snapshot is intentionally limited to deployed runtime source, deployment inputs, and two verification inputs. It is not an export of every repository file and does not survive simultaneous deletion of both the GitHub repository and Vercel project.
No recoverable external player-save copy exists in V0.8.2.
This round uses browser engines and mobile viewports, not a controlled physical iPhone installation.

An in-repository workflow cannot prove that it will run after an authorized user deletes or disables that same workflow. Tamper-proof bootstrap enforcement requires an external GitHub ruleset or required workflow that is not configured here.

requirements.condition: The baseline commit and tree resolve exactly, git fsck passes, and the baseline uses neither Git LFS nor submodules.
GitHub retains an archive branch at the exact baseline commit and the review branch contains a self-contained SHA-256-bound snapshot, so the mutable archive ref is not the only retained copy.
The snapshot manifest contains exactly 20 non-duplicated bindings: 16 deployed runtime source files, two deployment inputs, and two verification inputs, each byte-identical to the baseline tree.
Every canonical claim names this as a deployed browser-runtime source and deployment-input byte checkpoint and explicitly avoids a whole-repository or player-save backup claim.

The remote archive ref resolves exactly to the baseline commit, and a clean GitHub checkout of that immutable SHA passes the independently retained verification kit through CATS_BASELINE_DIR; historical descendants do not depend on the mutable ref.
The historical baseline Vercel deployment is READY and reports the exact baseline commit.
The historical deployment, current fixed Production deployment, and fresh recovery deployment are separately named identities and are not conflated.
All 17 fixed-Production manifest paths have the expected HTTP status, MIME type, byte length, and SHA-256.

Authenticated connected-project Vercel metadata reports the fresh READY deployment at the witnessed single-parent no-content commit whose tree is exactly the baseline tree; sealed response captures prove all 15 non-HTML responses match directly and each HTML response equals exact baseline bytes followed by exactly one captured deployment-bound Preview Toolbar suffix. The connector response is not cryptographically signed, so independent critics must re-query that deployment before C2.

The fresh Preview evidence preserves safe response headers and the raw base64 response for each normalized HTML path so its observed and normalized SHA-256 can be recalculated without a share credential.
The recovered runtime completes the deterministic 1F-through-10F loop in Chromium and WebKit at 390x844 and 375x667.
Without qa=1 and with normal motion, a player can start, enter battle, and reload successfully in Chromium and WebKit at both mobile viewports.

With service workers enabled in Chromium at both viewports, the test verifies controller acquisition, the exact 15 cache keys and response-body hashes, obsolete and synthetic future cache removal, and offline shell restart.
Normal reload preserves all 19 durable fields and four screen fields checked by CI, while the known live-roster non-persistence remains reproduced and disclosed rather than hidden.
Schema-2 durable state reloads and the raw future-schema localStorage string remains byte-for-byte unmodified.

Final-size visual and written evidence makes the checkpoint purpose and the roster, deleted-save, physical-device, and product-quality boundaries understandable without implying those limitations are solved.
Every persisted local raw report and all six 390x844 final-size visual records have verifier-checked SHA-256 and expected dimensions or report fields.

Exact-head C1 CI produces the acceptance CI record added only at C2; exact-head C2 CI produces the candidate CI record added only at C3. The C3 workflow binds all three records to immutable run-level identity, head SHA and head branch, checkout tree, API job timestamps, successful required job steps, artifact metadata, downloaded ZIP digest, and role-specific entry count. No field under the historical Actions run pull_requests[] relationship is an authority. The original raw-source record instead binds its synthetic merge SHA, tree, ordered parents, exact job-log merge ref, and all ten raw ZIP members. Each new C1/C2 artifact contains one duplicate-key-free, hash-bound event-time ci-provenance.json member whose exact raw UTF-8 bytes are committed in the next CI record and bind the event-time PR number, refs and SHAs, primary checkout, verification kit, served runtime, run identity, and actual workflow ref/commit/blob. C3 PR-head CI and the resulting main push CI artifacts are downloaded and subjected to the same provenance inspection as external completion conditions.

Each expiring CI artifact records its ID, digest, size, file count, expiry, and—where required—the exact ci-provenance.json member hash, and is present and unexpired when the C3 workflow verifies the seal. Later descendants rely on the sealed Git history, ten committed raw reports, self-contained snapshot, and browser re-execution from the immutable C3 kit rather than artifact retention.

After C1 CI, three procedurally independent critics review exact C1 and their records are added in C2; the runtime critic must also re-query and bind the fresh Vercel deployment. After exact-head C2 CI, a separate final judge reviews C2, its three critic records, and C2 CI. Every review records its assigned task path, assignment, target-specific verbatim JSON response, method, findings, target, and zero unresolved material blockers; both outer records and embedded verbatim JSON reject duplicate object keys.
No original game runtime, asset, PWA, or deployment-input byte changes during the Step 1A redo.
README, AGENTS, MASTER_SPEC, FLOORS_1_10_DESIGN, PROJECT_HANDOVER, PROJECT_STATUS, and BASELINE_V082 agree exactly on Step 1A and later-step states and contain no retired ambiguous checkpoint name.

C1 freezes Acceptance revision 4, the validator, workflow, external artifact verifier, snapshot contract, capture script, Round 3 failure record, prior Acceptance bytes, and durable evidence before its CI and before C2 review. Every JSON document consumed by the validator, including embedded reviewer responses, external inspection records, and ci-provenance raw bytes, must use an unambiguous duplicate-key-free representation.

C2 is the single-parent direct child of C1 and changes exactly the C1 CI evidence, clean-recovery evidence, and three critic records. C3 is the single-parent direct child of C2 and changes exactly the C2 CI evidence, final-judge and round records, plus the defined mechanical status transforms. Protected blobs keep their C1 hashes at C2 and C3, and an all-reachable-commit/all-parent-edge scan finds C3 as the only introduction of round-004.json.
Round 2 and Round 3 remain recorded as FAIL with their material blockers and are never rewritten into successes.

commitProtocol.c1: Acceptance checkpoint: status remains IN_PROGRESS; evaluator, workflow, snapshot, capture, and durable evidence are frozen before clean-checkout CI.
commitProtocol.c2: Review candidate: single-parent direct child of C1; only acceptance-ci-run.json, clean-recovery.json, and three C1 critic records change; status remains IN_PROGRESS. Exact-head C2 CI must pass before the final judge runs.
commitProtocol.c3: Audit seal: single-parent direct child of C2; only candidate-ci-run.json, the final-judge record, round-004.json, and acceptance-defined mechanical status transforms change.
commitProtocol.sealDiscovery: C3 is the unique single-parent commit in the complete reachable DAG whose tree contains quality-reviews/step-1-legacy-baseline/round-004.json while none of its parent trees contains that path. Discovery enumerates every commit and parent edge and does not use history-simplified path log output.
commitProtocol.futureMode: When the current repository workflow invokes it on a descendant of C3, the immutable Acceptance kernel remains the sole machine authority. Verification requires both sealed evidence trees, all exact universal quality-loop mirror claims, the duplicate-key-free authoritative Step 1A JSON entry with its canonical order, name, and PASS status, and one structured PASS marker and checklist row in each canonical document, then re-runs the historical C3 verifier against the immutable baseline. Arbitrary natural-language semantic completeness is not claimed, and preventing deletion or short-circuiting of the workflow itself requires an external GitHub ruleset that is not configured at audit time.
commitProtocol.mergePolicy: C1, C2, and C3 commit identities must be preserved; squash and rebase merge are forbidden for this PR.

futureRequiredQualityGateClaims: この規則は、仕様書、調査、画像、画面、コード、QA、配信など、ユーザーへ成果として渡す全作業へ適用する。
一つでも不合格なら`IN_PROGRESS`へ戻し、失敗原因を次のAcceptanceへ加えて手順1から再構成する。
`PASS`時だけ完成報告する。未完成時は完成したように表現しない。
それ以外は内部で①〜④を繰り返し、合格後にまとめて報告する。
ユーザーが品質を否認した場合は旧判定を守らず、直ちに`IN_PROGRESS`へ戻して次roundの失敗条件へ反映する。

futureNormativeKernel.authorityRetention: The full quality-reviews/step-1-legacy-baseline Git tree is immutable at descendants of C3 when the verifier runs, so this kernel cannot be overridden by a current Markdown edit.
futureNormativeKernel.qualityLoopAuthority: futureRequiredQualityGateClaims is the non-overridable machine-readable minimum; current QUALITY_GATE.md is an evolvable mirror that must retain every exact claim.
futureNormativeKernel.step1StatusAuthority: The sealed PROJECT_STATUS legacyBaseline and legacyV082Verification objects plus the exact preparation[0] object {order:1,name:legacy-v082-source-runtime-byte-checkpoint,status:PASS} are authoritative; that entry must be unique by name and order, and current canonical Markdown files must retain one structured PASS marker and checklist row.
futureNormativeKernel.jsonAuthorityEncoding: Every JSON document consumed by the verifier, including PROJECT_STATUS, Acceptance, CI, round, evidence, critic, judge, and embedded verbatimResponse JSON, must reject duplicate object keys before semantic validation.
futureNormativeKernel.boundary: The verifier does not claim to understand every possible contradictory natural-language sentence. Such prose cannot override this frozen kernel or structured JSON status, and later human review remains responsible for editorial clarity.

sealStatusTransforms.markdownRule: For each canonical Markdown file, every listed from value must occur exactly once in C2. Applying the ordered replacements must reproduce the C3 blob byte-for-byte; no unlisted edit is allowed and status-vocabulary definitions remain unchanged.

ciProvenanceContract.runHeadAuthority: The Actions run-level id, attempt, workflow, event, head_sha, and head_branch are the historical run authority. No field under the related pull_requests[] array, including number, refs, or SHAs, is used as historical authority.
ciProvenanceContract.eventTimeAuthority: For new C1/C2 runs, the primary checkout step immediately captures the event-specific context, exact HEAD/tree, run identity, github.workflow_ref, github.workflow_sha, and actual workflow blob before resolving another kit or executing repository test code. A second step only appends the verification-kit and served-runtime identities. The final raw bytes are copied without regeneration into the artifact and then into the next immutable CI record, bound by member SHA-256 and provider artifact digest.
ciProvenanceContract.claimBoundary: ci-provenance.json is generated by the frozen workflow from GitHub event context and the checked-out Git objects. It is not a GitHub-signed attestation; trust comes from the frozen generator, exact-head workflow execution, downloaded artifact digest, durable raw-byte copy, and cross-checks against run/job APIs.

externalArtifactVerifier.output: machine-readable PASS summary binding run, attempt, job, artifact, event, head, artifact digest, provenance SHA-256, verification kit, and served runtime

reviewAuthenticity.verbatimResponseContract: Each reviewer must return one JSON object that binds its role, exact target commit and tree, CI run and job, verdict, material blockers, method, and findings to the outer record. The runtime critic must additionally bind its post-C1 Vercel deployment re-query; the final judge must bind the three critic-record hashes.
reviewAuthenticity.machineVerificationBoundary: The validator proves internal record, hash, target, ordering, and cross-reference consistency only. It cannot prove reviewer identity or independence.
reviewAuthenticity.reason: The collaboration reviewers are separate agent executions with distinct assigned roles, but their responses are transcribed and committed by the primary agent and are not cryptographically signed. The final report must describe this as procedural independence only.

externalMetadataAuthenticity.mitigation: Freeze the exact C1 metadata record, independently re-query the fresh deployment after C1, bind that check in the runtime critic's target-specific verbatim response, and separately verify the sealed raw deployment responses.
externalMetadataAuthenticity.claimBoundary: This is procedurally cross-checked provider metadata plus recalculable response evidence, not a cryptographically signed Vercel attestation.
